desc:
A match is a triple (i, j, len) with len ≥ 1 such that the substring of s that starts at index i and has length len is equal to the substring of t that starts at index j and has the same length. Different triples count as different matches even when they spell the same text.

Return the total number of matches.

s = "aab", t = "ab"   ->  4   ("a" at s[0] and s[1] vs t[0], "b" vs t[1], and "ab" at s[1] vs t[0])
s = "aaa", t = "aa"   ->  8   (6 pairs of single letters + 2 pairs of "aa")
constraints: Both strings contain only lowercase English letters
The answer is below 2<sup>31</sup> for every allowed input
hints: Checking every triple by comparing the substrings is far too slow. Fix the end of the two substrings instead of their start.
Let E(i, j) be the number of matches whose substrings end at s[i] and t[j]. If s[i] != t[j] there are none.

If the characters are equal, a match ending here is either the single letter pair, or a match ending at (i-1, j-1) extended by one. So E(i, j) = E(i-1, j-1) + 1, and the answer is the sum of all E values.
editorial: Group the matches by where the two substrings end. A match ending at positions (i, j) requires s[i] == t[j]. Its length is 1, or it is a match ending at (i-1, j-1) with one more equal character appended. Hence E[i][j] = E[i-1][j-1] + 1 when the characters are equal and 0 otherwise, and every match is counted exactly once at its end pair.

The longest common substring problem uses the same table but takes the maximum; here every cell contributes to a sum. Only the previous row is needed, so the memory is O(t.length). The total fits in 32 bits for the stated limits (the worst case is two strings of one repeated letter, about n<sup>3</sup>/3).
solution:
def countMatchingSubstrings(s, t):
    n = len(t)
    prev = [0] * (n + 1)
    total = 0
    for i in range(len(s)):
        cur = [0] * (n + 1)
        c = s[i]
        for j in range(n):
            if c == t[j]:
                v = prev[j] + 1
                cur[j + 1] = v
                total += v
        prev = cur
    return total
